chapterTitle: Chapter 3: Singular and Plural (एकवचन और बहुवचन) 🍎🍏
learningGoals: Understand the concept of Singular (एक - One) and Plural (अनेक - Many). 🔢
Learn the basic rule of adding 's' to make a naming word plural (e.g., boy -> boys). ➕
Learn the rule of adding 'es' for words ending in ch, sh, s, x, or o. 📝
Identify singular and plural words in everyday conversations. 🗣️
Write simple sentences using correct plural forms. ✍️
conversationStarters: I have one apple, but you have three. How do we say 'three apple' correctly? 🍎
When we have many boxes, do we add an 's' or an 'es' at the end? 📦
Can you show me 'one' finger, and now show me 'many' fingers? 🖐️
teachingTips: Explain in Hindi: 'जब कोई चीज़ एक होती है तो वह Singular (एकवचन) है, और एक से ज़्यादा होने पर Plural (बहुवचन) बन जाती है।' 💡
Use physical objects like pencils. Hold up one and say 'pencil', hold up three and say 'pencils'. ✏️
For words like brush, box, and potato, emphasize the sound when adding 'es' so they hear the difference. 🔊
Make intentional mistakes like 'Look at those two dog' and let your child correct you to 'dogs'. 😂
Create flashcards with singular on one side and plural on the other side. 📇

funActivities.title: The 'S' and 'ES' Magic Wand 🪄
funActivities.description: Give your child a pencil to act as a magic wand. Say a singular word like 'Car' or 'Fox'. They must tap the wand and say the plural magic word ('Cars', 'Foxes').

funActivities.title: Plural Scavenger Hunt 🧺
funActivities.description: Ask your child to find 'one book', 'two shoes', and 'three toys' in the house and bring them to you, saying the plural words aloud.

funActivities.title: Drawing One and Many 🖍️
funActivities.description: Fold a paper in half. On one side, write 'One' and have them draw a flower. On the other side, write 'Many' and have them draw flowers.
